subject: What Changed to Your Credit Card Today? Edition 16
summary: ICICI Bank raises its branch cash credit card bill payment fee from ₹100 to ₹150 plus GST, and two Canara Bank card pages add an MDR disclosure link that changes nothing for cardholders.
body_html:
What Changed to Your Credit Card Today?

Edition 16, 17 October 2026

If you still clear your credit card bill by walking into a bank branch with cash, this one is for you, and I want to say first that there is nothing silly about it. Plenty of people do it because they get paid in cash, or because they do not fully trust an app with a large payment. It is a perfectly normal habit. It also just got more expensive at ICICI Bank, so let's work out by how much and what I would do about it.

ICICI Bank: Credit Card Bill Payment (cash at branch)

What changed. ICICI's bill payment page used to say that paying at a branch, or depositing cash, carried a fee of ₹100 plus GST. It now says ₹150 plus 18% GST per payment transaction. The bank appears to have updated this on its official page; we haven't found independent confirmation yet, so treat it as what the page says today, not as a circular we have seen.

The math. GST at 18% on ₹100 is ₹18, so you used to pay ₹118 per cash deposit. Now GST on ₹150 is ₹27, so you pay ₹177. That is ₹59 more every time, a 50% jump.

  • Pay cash once a month: ₹1,416 a year before, ₹2,124 now. Extra: ₹708.
  • Pay cash twice a month, say a salary-cycle payment and a mid-month top-up: ₹2,832 before, ₹4,248 now. Extra: ₹1,416.

On a ₹30,000 monthly bill, even the old fee was about 0.4%. The new one is about 0.6%. Small per payment, but it is money buying you nothing.

The catch. This is a fee on the way you pay, not on the card, so it hits you whichever ICICI card you hold. And the page lists UPI, the iMobile app and the debit card at an ICICI ATM as ways to pay, none of which show a branch-cash style fee in the text we compared.

What I'd do. Move the bill to UPI or the iMobile app. If your income is in cash, deposit it into your own bank account once, then pay the card digitally. You save ₹177 a payment, and you get a digital record that your payment landed on time, which protects your CIBIL score.

Canara Bank: a new link, not a new benefit

Two Canara Bank card pages, the Mastercard Gold Secured and the Rupay Select, picked up a new line reading "MDR on RuPay Credit Card Transactions through UPI". MDR (merchant discount rate) is the fee a shop pays to accept a digital payment. It sits among footer links such as the investor calendar and grievance redressal, so it looks like a bank-wide disclosure link, not a change to what you earn, pay or get on either card. Our system flagged it, but I would not change anything because of it, and we have not found independent confirmation of anything beyond the link itself.

What I'd actually do with this

One clear call: if you pay by branch cash, stop. Switch to UPI or the app this month; it takes ten minutes to set up and saves you ₹708 to ₹1,416 a year at the new fee. For the Canara cards, do nothing. Nothing about your rewards or fees changed in the text we compared.

This is my honest read, not formal financial advice. I'm not your advisor, and before you act on anything big, run it past a professional. But here's exactly how I'd think about it: small fees repeat, and repeated fees are the ones worth killing. You're smart, and you'll make the right call.

Monzy
